i35-south-austin.displayName: I-35 South (San Antonio to Austin, TX)
i35-south-austin.lengthNote: Haversine length of the modeled 25-vertex i35.geojson polyline (~121.7 km / ~75.6 mi). The real signed I-35 driving distance from downtown San Antonio to downtown Austin is roughly 79 mi / 127 km; the modeled coarse polyline runs slightly short of that. Treat as modeled/estimated, not a surveyed value.

sections.name: Downtown San Antonio (I-35 / I-10 / I-37 downtown interchanges)
sections.notes: Urban core through downtown San Antonio with tightly spaced ramps and the I-10/I-35 and I-35/I-37 interchanges. 60 mph is a typical Texas urban-freeway posting but was NOT confirmed against an official TxDOT sign inventory for this exact segment. Lane count approximate. No HOV/managed lanes exist here.

sections.name: Northeast San Antonio to Selma / Schertz (through Live Oak, Universal City)
sections.notes: Suburban San Antonio, 8-10 general-purpose lanes in places. 65 mph estimated; not verified. No HOV/managed lanes. Retail/interchange density around Selma and Schertz.

sections.name: Schertz / Cibolo to New Braunfels
sections.notes: Transitional suburban-to-open freeway. 70 mph estimated; some open Texas stretches are posted up to 75 mph but the exact per-subsegment posting was not verified. No managed lanes.

sections.name: New Braunfels to San Marcos
sections.notes: Open freeway between the two river towns. 70 mph estimated; not verified. Recurring weekend/tuber and outlet-mall traffic near the San Marcos Premium Outlets. No managed lanes.

sections.name: San Marcos through Kyle and Buda (Hays County commuter belt)
sections.notes: One of the fastest-growing commuter stretches in Texas; frequent recurring congestion around Kyle and Buda. 65 mph estimated; not verified. No managed lanes today. This segment falls within/near the limits of TxDOT's future I-35 Capital Express South managed-lane project (see hovRule).

sections.name: Buda to South Austin (Slaughter Ln / Ben White Blvd / SH 71)
sections.notes: Freeway densifies approaching Austin. 60 mph estimated; not verified. ACTIVE construction zone: TxDOT I-35 Capital Express South is building elevated managed (HOV) lanes here between SH 71/Ben White and SH 45 SE (targeted completion ~late 2028). No managed lanes are OPEN to traffic today (hovLanes = 0).

sections.name: Central / Downtown Austin (SH 71/Ben White to US 290 E, Lady Bird Lake)
sections.notes: Downtown Austin I-35 with upper/lower decks near the Lady Bird Lake bridge and closely spaced frontage-road ramps; one of Texas's most notorious congestion points. 60 mph estimated; not verified. ACTIVE construction: TxDOT I-35 Capital Express Central (~$5.6B, work began early 2025, ~2033 completion) is rebuilding this ~8-mile segment and adding two non-tolled HOV managed lanes per direction. None are OPEN yet (hovLanes = 0).

hovRule.notes: As of mid-2026 I-35 itself carries NO open HOV/managed lanes on the San Antonio-Austin corridor, so hovLanes is modeled as 0 on every section. This is VERIFIED as an under-construction, not-yet-open situation: TxDOT's I-35 Capital Express Central project (US 290 E to SH 71/Ben White, work started early 2025, ~2033 finish) and Capital Express South project (SH 71/Ben White to SH 45 SE, ~late 2028 finish) will EACH add two non-tolled high-occupancy-vehicle managed lanes per direction. When open these will be the corridor's first I-35 HOV lanes. Important disambiguation: the well-known Austin MoPac (Loop 1) Express Lanes are a DIFFERENT road (a tolled variable-price managed lane on Loop 1, run by the Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority) and are NOT on I-35. Do not attribute MoPac's managed lanes to I-35.

bottlenecks.name: Downtown Austin I-35 (upper/lower decks, Lady Bird Lake to US 290 E)
bottlenecks.locationDesc: Central Austin I-35 through downtown, roughly SH 71/Ben White north to US 290 East; the double-decked segment over/near Lady Bird Lake.
bottlenecks.reason: Perennially ranked among Texas's (and the nation's) worst freeway bottlenecks: 1950s-era double-deck design, frontage-road weaving, no shoulders in places, and metro-wide commuter plus I-35 through-freight volumes converging on downtown. Now compounded by the multi-year Capital Express Central reconstruction. Assigned near-maximum severity.

bottlenecks.name: Buda / Kyle (Hays County) commuter squeeze
bottlenecks.locationDesc: I-35 through Buda and Kyle, roughly the FM 1626 / Kyle Pkwy / Buda area south of Austin (near [-97.841, 30.083]).
bottlenecks.reason: Explosive suburban growth in Hays County funnels a large commuter volume onto a 6-lane freeway section, producing heavy recurring AM/PM peak congestion and queue spillback. High severity reflects growth outpacing capacity ahead of the Capital Express South widening.

bottlenecks.name: San Marcos (outlet malls / river-recreation traffic)
bottlenecks.locationDesc: I-35 through San Marcos near the Premium/Tanger outlet centers and the university/river area (near [-97.941, 29.883]).
bottlenecks.reason: Interchange-dense segment with major outlet-mall trip generation, Texas State University traffic, and heavy summer tubing/river-recreation peaks stacking onto through traffic. Recurring weekend and holiday congestion. Moderate-high severity.

bottlenecks.name: New Braunfels (Comal / Schlitterbahn corridor)
bottlenecks.reason: Regional tourism draw (Comal/Guadalupe rivers, Schlitterbahn) plus growing bedroom-community commuting between San Antonio and Austin creates recurring weekend and peak congestion where the freeway narrows. Moderate severity.

i35-south-austin.tolls: The I-35 mainlanes between San Antonio and Austin are NOT tolled and are free to drive. The primary tolled ALTERNATIVE is SH 130 (State Highway 130), a ~91-mile toll road running east and south of Austin that parallels I-35 as a bypass; its southern section (SH 130 South, roughly SH 45 SE in Mustang Ridge to I-10 in Seguin, ~41 mi) is privately operated with all-electronic cashless tolling and a posted speed limit up to 85 mph. Operators advertise substantial time savings versus I-35 in this corridor. Exact SH 130 toll PRICES vary by class/segment and payment method (TxTag/toll-tag vs pay-by-mail, with tag customers paying materially less) and were NOT verified to a specific dollar amount here, so no rate is quoted. The future I-35 Capital Express managed (HOV) lanes are planned as NON-tolled. Do not confuse SH 130 (tolled bypass) with I-35 (free mainlanes).
i35-south-austin.waymoReality: Modeled actor on this corridor, not a real intercity-freeway deployment. VERIFIED: Waymo does operate a driverless robotaxi service in Austin, launched to the public via the Waymo-Uber partnership in early 2025 (Uber-app matching began March 2025; roughly 100 vehicles cited by mid-2025). That service is SURFACE-STREET ridehailing within an Austin operating zone, NOT operation on the intercity I-35 freeway between San Antonio and Austin. Waymo also runs in San Antonio as a separate metro service. There is no verified Waymo driverless service running the I-35 mainlanes San Antonio-to-Austin as an intercity route; corridor-level 'Waymo' behavior in this model should be treated as simulated. (Consistent with the other corridors' note that Waymo paused all freeway rides in May 2026 pending a construction-zone software update.)
i35-south-austin.disclaimer: VERIFIED vs MODELED. Verified from cited sources: (1) I-35 currently has NO open HOV/managed lanes on the San Antonio-Austin corridor; TxDOT's Capital Express Central (US 290 E to SH 71/Ben White, started early 2025, ~2033) and Capital Express South (SH 71/Ben White to SH 45 SE, ~2028) projects will each ADD two non-tolled HOV managed lanes per direction, none open yet -> hovLanes modeled as 0; (2) the Austin MoPac/Loop 1 Express Lanes are a separate tolled road, not I-35; (3) the I-35 mainlanes are non-tolled and SH 130 is the tolled parallel bypass (up to 85 mph, all-electronic tolling); (4) downtown Austin I-35 is a top-tier notorious bottleneck and the San Marcos/Kyle/Buda stretch is heavily congested and growing; (5) Waymo runs a real driverless surface-street robotaxi service in Austin via the Uber partnership (public since 2025) but not as an I-35 intercity-freeway operation. MODELED / ESTIMATED (not surveyed): the corridor length (haversine over a coarse hand-placed polyline; ~75.6 mi modeled vs ~79 mi real driving distance); ALL posted speed limits (every section has speedLimitVerified=false - values are typical Texas urban/rural interstate postings, NOT confirmed against an official TxDOT sign inventory); all per-section lane counts (approximate); and every bottleneck severityIndex (0..1 values assigned as relative congestion judgments, not measured). Named geojson waypoint coordinates are real; intermediate polyline vertices are approximated to follow the alignment. Do not treat estimated values as authoritative for engineering or legal purposes.
